body:
## Summary

Closes #8.

This PR makes the SPA the first-class deliverable and now implements the reviewer-requested repository layout literally: JavaScript code and JS tooling live under `js/`, and the Rust workspace lives under `rust/`. The public web app publishes through GitHub Pages, the README starts with the browser-first user flow, and the case study records the issue, PR feedback, requirements, research, and implementation plan.

## What changed

### R-L1..R-L5 — Browser publishing

- `js/scripts/build-pages.mjs` builds `dist/pages/` from `js/src/web/`, writes `404.html`, `.nojekyll`, `manifest.webmanifest`, and injects the manifest link into a copied `index.html`.
- `.github/workflows/pages.yml` uses the official Pages stack: `actions/configure-pages@v5`, `actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3`, and `actions/deploy-pages@v4`; PRs build only, `main` deploys and smoke-tests the published URL.
- `js/tests/build-pages.test.js` covers the Pages artifact contract.

### R-L6..R-L8 — User-first docs

- `README.md` now starts with “Try it now”, then local Rust server, JavaScript fallback, and server discovery.
- `docs/USER-GUIDE.md` documents the install-nothing web flow, Rust server, JS fallback, desktop/mobile shells, sync, backup/import, and troubleshooting.

### R-L9 — Server parity audit

- `docs/SERVER-PARITY.md` compares `js/src/server/` with `rust/crates/meta-sovereign-server/` route by route.
- Current audit remains explicit: Rust covers the browser-first user flows, while six operator-hardening endpoints are JS-only and documented with JS fallback paths.

### R-L10..R-L12 — Requested layout + CI paths

- Moved JavaScript source, tests, scripts, examples, experiments, CLI entrypoint, Electron shell, and ESLint config under `js/`.
- Moved `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, and `crates/` under `rust/`.
- Updated package exports, bin path, npm scripts, Deno config, Dockerfiles, GitHub Actions, release/docs scripts, tests, and docs to use the new paths.
- Updated the changeset to describe the new `js/` and `rust/` layout.

### R-L13..R-L15 — Case study

- `docs/case-studies/issue-8/` contains requirements, solution plan, components survey, external research, CI/CD template comparison, raw issue payloads, and raw PR feedback payloads.
- `docs/REQUIREMENTS.md` section L now marks each R-L requirement with the current status.

## How to verify

```bash
npm run build:web
npm run build:pages
npm test
npm run check
bash js/scripts/check-mjs-syntax.sh
bash js/scripts/check-file-line-limits.sh
npm run docs:api
cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all --check
cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace
```

Local results in this work session:

- `npm run build:pages` wrote 16 files to `dist/pages/`.
- `npm test` passed 175/175 tests.
- `npm run check` passed ESLint, Prettier, and jscpd.
- `cargo test --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace` passed all Rust tests and doctests.
- Root no longer contains `src/`, `scripts/`, `tests/`, `bin/`, `electron/`, `examples/`, `experiments/`, `crates/`, `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, or `eslint.config.js`.

## Post-merge checks

- Pages deploy should publish <https://link-foundation.github.io/meta-sovereign/> from `main`.
- The changeset should prepare the next minor release.
title: Browser-first publishing with js/rust layout split (R-L1..R-L15)
